About a month ago, I suddenly felt like I could do everything—rearrange my entire studio, start composing again after years, even launch an online course. I wasn’t sleeping much, maybe five hours a night, but I didn’t feel tired. I snapped at my husband over tiny things, then minutes later I’d feel this intense rush of joy, like I was glowing. But that high didn’t last. I started feeling reckless, like signing up for things without thinking, and convinced I could perform at a professional level again, even though I haven’t practiced seriously in years.

Then, two weeks ago, it just collapsed. I couldn’t feel anything—no joy in music, no connection to my students. I cried once, but mostly I just felt hollow. I started thinking I was a burden, that my teaching was pointless, and one night I filled a glass with pills but stopped myself. I told no one. Now I’m just… tired. I can’t focus during lessons. My mind races sometimes, but I can’t tell if that’s from anxiety or something else. I don’t know when any of this started—whether it’s new or if I’ve always felt this way and didn’t notice.
D008-D003_h020.options:
A. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder
D008-D003_h020.answer: B & A. Bipolar I Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D008-D003_h021.question:
I’ve been struggling for the past few months—maybe closer to five now—just feeling completely out of sync with myself. There was this two-month stretch not too long ago where I was on fire—coding late into the night, starting three different side projects, feeling like I could take over the tech world. I wasn’t really sleeping, but I didn’t feel tired. I felt… invincible. I went on a dating spree, hooking up with people I barely knew, which isn’t like me at all. I didn’t care about the risks.  

But then it crashed. Hard. The last three months have been the opposite. I can’t get motivated to open my laptop. I used to love gaming, building apps for fun—now I just stare at the wall. I wake up at 3 a.m. every night and can’t fall back asleep. I’ve been forgetting simple things—where I left my keys, deadlines at work. My focus is shot.  

Sometimes, when I’m on the balcony or crossing the street, this sudden urge hits me—like I should just step forward, not because I want to die, but because the thought appears out of nowhere, intense and jarring. I don’t act on it, but it scares me.  

I’ve always been kind of restless, but I’m not sure if that’s new or just how I’ve always been.
D008-D003_h021.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder
D008-D003_h021.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D008-D003_h022.question:
I’ve been feeling all over the place for the past few months—like I’m riding two different storms. About two months back, I was on this high where I couldn’t sit still. I suddenly wanted to fix every damn thing on the boat, worked 18-hour shifts without feeling tired, and felt invincible, like the ocean couldn’t touch me. I even called an old flame out of nowhere and ended up meeting her—things got out of hand. It wasn’t like me at all; my wife still won’t talk to me about it.  

Then it just crashed. For the past three months, I’ve been pulling away—from my crew, my wife, even dinner at home feels like too much. I lie awake most nights, drenched in sweat from these awful dreams—sharks circling the boat, my body sinking into the dark. Choosing what to eat, what shirt to wear—it all freezes me up. Some mornings, I whisper, “Just don’t wake up,” not because I’d hurt myself, but because it all feels too heavy.  

The energy comes and goes, but I can’t say if it’s always been this way since I was a kid—I just know it’s wrecking my life now. Sometimes I’m moving fast, talking fast, but I can’t tell if that’s mania or just how a fisherman survives the sea.
D008-D003_h022.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder
D008-D003_h022.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D008-D003_h023.question:
For the past couple of months, I’ve felt like I’m on a rollercoaster I can’t get off. There were times—especially around work deadlines—when I suddenly felt unstoppable. I’d stay out late, go to parties I wouldn’t normally attend, say yes to people I barely knew. One night, I ended up sleeping with someone after meeting them just hours before. That’s not me. I don’t know what came over me—just this surge of confidence, of *wanting*, like I was invincible. But by morning, the guilt crashed in, and I’d snap into irritability over tiny things—a colleague’s tone, traffic, anything.

Before that, though, things were dark for months. I stopped replying to texts. My friends stopped inviting me out. I’d wake up at 3 a.m. every night, heart racing, and just lie there, unable to go back to sleep. Even picking what to wear felt impossible—like each decision carried huge weight. I started thinking about… well, what if I just wasn’t here? I imagined driving into a bridge barrier late at night when no one’s around. Not because I wanted to die, exactly, but because it felt like the only decision I could control.

Now I don’t know if I’m burned out, broken, or just… stuck. My mind races sometimes, but I can’t tell if that’s always been this way or if it started recently.
D008-D003_h023.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder
D008-D003_h023.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D008-D003_h024.question:
I’m 55, and I’ve been doing pest control work for over 30 years—mostly solitary, getting from job to job. Since I’ve been divorced, it’s just me and the truck. About three months ago, I hit a rough patch. I couldn’t get excited about anything—not the job, not seeing my kids, not even the fishing I used to love. I’d sleep eight hours and still feel drained, like I hadn’t slept at all. I used to make quick calls on the job, but now I’d sit in the parking lot, arguing with myself about which trap to use. And some days… I just thought, “What’s the point? I’d rather not wake up.” No plan, just that thought, over and over.

Before that, though, I was the opposite—jacked up, like I’d been wired. I didn’t need sleep. I was going nonstop—taking extra jobs, talking to strangers, even hooked up with two different women in one week, which isn’t me. Felt invincible. Now I’m stuck in this limbo, bouncing between wanting to vanish and wondering if I’ll snap back into that reckless version of myself. I don’t know which me is real anymore.
D008-D003_h024.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder
D008-D003_h024.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D008-D003_h025.question:
I’m 56, a partner at a midsize firm—been practicing law for over 30 years. Since my divorce five years ago, things have been off, but last winter was the worst. For about two months, I was wired—sleeping three hours a night, not tired, just *on*. I took on four new clients, started two side ventures, even put down a deposit on a restaurant no one thought through. My partner pulled me aside—said I was snapping at associates over typos, pacing meetings, talking over everyone. I knew it was reckless, but it felt like momentum. Then it crashed.

For the next three months, I couldn’t get out of bed. Work piled up. I’d sit at my desk, fully dressed, staring at the same sentence for an hour. My head felt thick, like I was thinking through cotton. Slept eight hours, sometimes more, but woke up exhausted. I started thinking, “Wouldn’t it be easier if I just didn’t wake up?” Not planning anything—just… tired. Now I’m back at work, but I can’t tell if I’m still depressed or if I’m just waiting for the next time I lose control. The energy scares me—was that mania, or am I just impulsive under stress? I don’t remember being like this as a kid.
D008-D003_h025.options:
A. Delusional Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
    D. Bipolar I Disorder
D008-D003_h025.answer: D & C. Bipolar I Disorder & Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
